currentDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann aus Metallabscheidungen und Messungen einfacher galvanischer Zellen eine verkürzte Redoxreihe erstellen und Donator-/Akzeptor-Paare kennzeichnen.
currentDescriptionEn: The learner can create a shortened redox series from metal depositions and measurements of simple galvanic cells and identify donor/acceptor pairs.
scope: Orientation for supplied metal-deposition observations and the represented Zn/Cu cell; no independent learner performance or practical experiment evidence.

independentVisualFindings.finding: The left Zn strip in the blue Cu2+ solution bears brown copper metal. The adjacent Cu strip in the transparent Ag+ solution bears grey silver metal. Labels distinguish Zn/Cu electrodes, dissolved Cu2+/Ag+ and metal/ion pairs. No label calls metallic Ag an electron acceptor. Cu2+ and Ag+ are the electron-accepting ions in these respective deposition reactions.

Zn > Cu > Ag is consistent with the shown metal donor-strength observations. Zn/Zn2+, Cu/Cu2+ and Ag/Ag+ are separately shown. This is an abbreviated contextual metal order, not the opposite ranking of the ions as electron acceptors.

The e-minus arrow lies on the external path from the left Zn electrode to the right Cu electrode. Both wires contact metal tops. The U-shaped salt bridge enters both solutions and has no electron arrow or metallic wire connection. The image is consistent with ionic charge compensation through the bridge; it does not explicitly demonstrate ion migration.

The Cu2+ beakers use clearly saturated blue; the Ag+ beaker is transparent neutral grey/white. The Zn2+ beaker is noticeably paler than Cu2+ and shares the illustration’s blue background/glass tint, without a stated blue-zinc chemistry observation. Its tint is read as schematic transparent styling. AgNO3 and ordinary aqueous zinc salts are not taught as intrinsically blue. The deposition cartoons do not specify complete final solution composition or reaction progress.

The meter displays +1.10 V for this depicted Zn/Cu example. That reading is chemically plausible and equals the familiar standard cell potential. No statement says every Zn/Cu cell must measure that voltage. Conditions are not given in the picture; it cannot supply a universal measured value, concentration-independent law, or fresh assessment data.

At 360px, the essential Zn, Cu, Cu2+, Ag+, Zn2+, electron-arrow label, Zn > Cu > Ag and all three metal/ion pair labels remain decipherable. Salt bridge and +1.10 V are also recognizable. At 680px the notation is clear. There is no crop. Two deposition beakers and the paired cell remain visually separable. Raised ionic charges, friendly outlines, copper/grey colors and the compact landscape layout fit an approachable comic style. No technical ID, watermark or unrelated topic is visible.

altText: Schematische Metallabscheidungen: Kupfer auf Zink in einer kupferionenhaltigen Lösung und Silber auf Kupfer in einer farblosen silberionenhaltigen Lösung. Daneben eine Zink-Kupfer-Zelle mit Salzbrücke, Messgerät und Elektronenrichtung im äußeren Leiter von Zink zu Kupfer. Die verkürzte Donatorreihenfolge Zn > Cu > Ag und die Paare Zn/Zn²⁺, Cu/Cu²⁺, Ag/Ag⁺ sind angegeben; Metall und zugehöriges Ion werden unterschieden.
altTextFinding: The alt text faithfully identifies copper on zinc, silver on copper, the colorless Ag+ reagent representation, the Zn/Cu cell, external Zn-to-Cu electron direction, abbreviated donor order and metal/ion pairs. It does not claim an independent experiment or call Ag metal the acceptor. It does not transcribe +1.10 V, so it should not be used as a numerical measurement record.
limits: An actual copper/silver-ion displacement creates Cu2+; as that product accumulates, the initially colorless solution can become blue. The transparent Ag+ cartoon is an orientation to the reagent/deposition relation, not proof that a complete post-reaction mixture always stays colorless.
+1.10 V is a particular example/standard-reference value. Actual cell readings depend on conditions. Assessment must provide separate case-specific measurements and conditions.
The abbreviated order refers to the metals as donors. The reverse ordering of corresponding metal ions as acceptors must not be inferred from the same greater-than line.
The image supports explanation; merely copying its pair legend or voltage does not demonstrate the learner’s ability to construct a redox series from fresh observations.

technicalEvidence.independentReRenderingReason: Actual frozen source and width views were visually inspected; their hashes match the recorded source/screenshots and the inspected capture script uses real Chromium with contain and the documented height cap. No unresolved representation risk required another capture.

primaryChemicalCrossChecks.supports: Zinc displaces copper metal from copper-ion solution; converse Cu/Zn2+ is not the corresponding spontaneous displacement.
Copper transfers electrons to Ag+ to form Ag metal and Cu2+; accumulated Cu2+ can color the mixture blue.
Zn-to-Cu external electron direction and approximately +1.10 V standard Zn/Cu cell; real nonstandard readings can differ.
